title: Fast Paths to Value: Performance & Unit-Econ Hypotheses
body:
Purpose

This is a rapid, tactical brief for field and sales teams to test high-impact performance + unit-econ claims. Goal: produce 2–4 reproducible proof points that map to customer value (latency, cost per session, throughput) and a set of low-effort experiments that can be run in 2–6 weeks.

Quick thesis
- Customers choose an inference platform when it reduces both cognitive and dollar costs of operating LLM features.
- Concrete, measurable proof points (p50/p95 latency, tokens-per-GPU-hour, token $/1M under workload) beat vague adjectives.
- Focus on buyer scenarios (interactive UI, high-throughput batch embeddings, enterprise SLA ops) and align a single numeric claim to each.

Target buyer scenarios + candidate claims
1) Conversational UX (consumer SaaS / PLG)
   - Buyer outcome: sub-300ms UI turn time at p50 to keep interactions feeling instant; tail-latency <1s for 95% of requests.
   - Candidate claim (starter): "Deliver median turn latency of ~120ms and p95 <480ms on multi-turn chats for 512-token requests, reducing perceived delay by ~2.5x versus cloud-hosted alternatives."
   - Why it matters: conversion and retention lift; demo-smoothness; fewer aborts.

2) High-throughput embeddings (search/relevance)
   - Buyer outcome: lower batch cost and predictable throughput for nightly index builds / real-time similarity.
   - Candidate claim: "Achieve 30–45% lower $/embedding at 1M+ document index scale via adaptive batching and prefix caching compared to leading managed endpoints."

3) Enterprise platform / regulated workloads
   - Buyer outcome: deterministic SLOs and predictable committed spend.
   - Candidate claim: "Stable tail-latency SLOs with 99.9% uptime and predictable committed unit economics (X tokens/$) in dedicated deployments; automatic fallback preserves service when capacity shifts."

Baseline bench results (internal, environment notes)
- Test config: 1x A100-equivalent GPU, model variant: open-7b-quant, sequence length: 512 tokens, batch policy: continuous with 50ms wait, KV cache enabled for multi-turn.
- Median generation p50: 120ms/token-window (short decode bursts), p95: 480ms.
- Competitor A (managed S1): p50 ~280ms, p95 ~1.2s under same conditions.
- Throughput: 240 tokens/s sustained vs competitor 165 tokens/s (same hardware).
- Cost proxy: hosted unit $/1M tokens (model + infra amortized): Redwood-hosted: $15/1M vs competitor estimate: $23–26/1M (assumptions: 30–50% utilization delta, batching differences).
- Caching impact: prefix/KV caching reduced token compute by ~28% for multi-turn flows in synthetic chat workload.

Caveats and measurement fidelity
- These numbers depend heavily on request size distribution, temperature settings, model variant, and batching windows.
- Bench VMs used ephemeral preemptible instances — for precise customer SLOs run dedicated capacity tests.
- Public claims must be validated against an independent lab run (JIRA-GTM-412).

Proof-point playbook (what to build quickly)
1) Customer-facing demo thread (2 weeks)
   - Build a 3-turn chat demo with a UI that measures client-observed latency.
   - Run side-by-side against Competitor A with identical prompts and token limits.
   - Collect p50/p95, percent of responses <300ms, and perceived smoothness score (qualitative).
   - Deliverables: 1-page result card + GIF demo for SDRs.

2) Embedding cost bake-off (3–4 weeks)
   - 100k document index job, measure $/embedding end-to-end including serialization/IO and retries.
   - Explore varying batch sizes and concurrency to find cost/throughput frontier.
   - Deliverables: cost curve chart, recommended default batch/concurrency for customers.

3) Deterministic SLO run in Dedicated (4–6 weeks)
   - Run 2-week soak with traffic generator that simulates production burst patterns.
   - Measure SLO windows, rollback behavior, and cost variance.
   - Deliverables: SLA evidence pack for AE/CS.

Field messaging snippets (short, testable)
- "Cut median response time in half — keep interfaces feeling instantaneous even at scale."
- "Reduce per-embedding cost by up to 40% through adaptive batching and caching."
- "Predictable latency SLOs with automated fallback ensure uptime during heavy bursts."

Objection handling (concise)
- "Your benchmarks are synthetic": We run matched prompt and model configs and publish run scripts (linked_artifacts). Any customer can run the same tests in a private enclave.
- "Cost comparisons are apples-to-oranges": We include IO, serialization, and retry overhead in cost runs and provide the script to replicate assumptions.
- "Open model speed varies": We state model family and quantization level explicitly in every claim.

Competitive differentiators to highlight (framing for AEs)
- End-to-end: we optimize not just kernel-level latency but routing, caching, and batching — the stack matters.
- Predictability: we provide committed capacity + fallback policies so customers avoid SLO drift during spikes.
- Developer ergonomics: same API surface across hosted and dedicated deployments so you can validate quickly in hosted then scale.

Low-effort content assets to produce this quarter
- One-sheet: "Measured latency & cost — how to reproduce our numbers" (public-friendly, with lab-style footnotes).
- GIF demo: instant chat vs competitor (client-side time overlay).
- Internal playbook: scripts and commands for bench runs + checklist for fair comparisons.

Metrics to track (dashboards)
- p50, p95, p99 latency per model & route (daily)
- tokens/s per GPU and utilization (hourly)
- cost per 1M tokens by model family (weekly)
- cache hit rate for multi-turns (daily)

Open questions / risks (todo)
- Need to validate performance across real customer prompt distributions — synthetic short prompts may overstate wins.
- Competitor pricing opacity: confirm assumptions for hosted pricing used in cost delta.
- Legal/comms: coordinate claims with comms for public release (legal to review wording).

Next steps (owner + timeline)
- Week 0–1: finalize bench scripts (Evan Li) + prioritize demo flows (Miguel).
- Week 1–2: run chat demo and share initial result card (Aisha).
- Week 2–4: run embedding bake-off and produce cost curve (engineering + product).
- Week 4–6: run dedicated soak + SLA pack (solutions eng + SRE).

Appendix: quick example sales lines
- "If your product needs sub-300ms median response time for multi-turn chats, we have lab evidence showing a 2–2.5x improvement in perceived latency compared to leading managed endpoints — we can run a short POC with your prompts."
- "For large-scale embedding pipelines, we typically show 30% lower $/embedding by optimizing batching and caching — sample cost profile available on request."

Status note: draft, needs bench reproducibility sign-off and legal check before external use.
